title: Asking for Directions
instructions: Describe a real or imagined route, then use feedback to improve your recording.
prompt: Describe a real or imagined place in a town. Say where it is, how to get there, and what polite question you would ask for help. Include one safety choice and a reason. Speak for about 75–105 seconds. Explain a planned route using going to and one safety rule using must or must not.
reference: I want to visit a small museum in my town. I start at the station. The museum is between the bakery and the restaurant, just past the market. I can ask a worker, “Excuse me, where is the museum?” The worker shows me a map. I walk straight along the street, cross at the signal, and turn right at the corner. Then I walk to the market; the museum is just past it. If the road is busy, I wait before I cross. I choose the signal because it helps me look for traffic. After the visit, I can rest on a bench near the station. We are going to take the shorter route past the bakery. We must cross at the signal and must not cross while the light is red. The event is free, so we do not have to buy tickets, but we should still arrive early.
